test_title: SSC Steno 2021 Official Paper (Held on: 15 Nov 2021 Shift 1
subject: general
question: Under the Goods and Services Tax (GST) regime, what is the highest tax slab as of August 2020?
solution:
The correct answer is __**28%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** percentage rates of tax levied on the sale of goods or services** under the CGST, SGST, and IGST Acts are referred to as** GST.**
 
• The GST rates for CGST and SGST (**for intra-state transactions) are nearly the same.**
 
• The GST rate for IGST (for inter-state transactions) is roughly** equal to the sum of the CGST and SGST rates**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The highest tax slab for the month of August 2020 was nearly about **28%.**
 
• The primary GST slabs for any regular taxpayers are presently pegged at** 0% (nil-rated), 5%, 12%, 18% & 28%. **
 
• There are a few GST rates that are less commonly utilised, such as 3% and 0.25%.
 
• Furthermore, the composition taxable people are required to pay GST at** lower or nominal rates, such as 1.5%. or 5% of their turnover**
